name: Modbus Client → Send
description: This action queues a custom Modbus frame for transmission and optionally handles the outcome.

config_entries.label: Address
config_entries.description: The Modbus device address the frame is sent to. Accepts `0`-`255`; the valid Modbus device range is `1`-`247`, and `0` is broadcast (no reply will ever arrive; see [Behavior](https://esphome.io/components/modbus_client#behavior)).

config_entries.label: Modbus ID
config_entries.description: The Modbus hub to send on. Automatically assigned when a single hub is configured.

config_entries.label: Pdu
config_entries.description: The PDU to send: function code followed by data. The device address and CRC are added automatically - do **not** include them. Maximum 253 bytes (the Modbus PDU limit): an empty or over-long YAML list fails config validation. As a lambda it must return a `modbus::helpers::PduBuffer` (a fixed-capacity stack vector, not `std::vector`): `return {0x03, 0x00, 0x10, 0x00, 0x01};` works, and so does directly returning the result of a `modbus::helpers::create_*_pdu()` builder - see [Building PDUs with Helpers](https://esphome.io/components/modbus_client#building-pdus-with-helpers). Unlike the YAML list, a lambda result isn't length-checked: one over 253 bytes is silently truncated to the limit rather than rejected. An empty lambda result (or a builder that fails - see below) also produces an empty PDU; the hub refuses to send it, and `on_not_sent` fires.
